newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares dip on profit-taking, no change seen.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares dip on profit-taking, no change seen.

text.p: Danish shares closed lower on Thursday after a morning of gains was wiped out by an afternoon of profit-taking, with dealers seeing Friday's market dependent on Wall Street with current price levels expected to hold.
"The dearth of buyers coupled with low turnover and profit-taking caused prices to drop. We should stick on current levels tomorrow depending on the U.S.," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index lost 1.07 point to close at 190.59 in overall bourse turnover of 1.166 billion crowns. The KFX August future fell 2.55 point to 191.45 with 1,001 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

SAS bucked the general downward trend, closing 7.5 percent or eight crowns higher at 114, bolstered by foreign buy recommendations, improved passenger volume and optimism about its future in the Star Alliance with Lufthansa and other major airlines.
Banks had a bad day with BG Bank shedding 15 crowns to close at 380, Den Danske dropping four to finish at 769 and Unidanmark losing seven crowns to end at 423.
